They can breathe fire like many of their descendants, however they also possess the ability to wield red lightning, which often manifests in the form of spears and glaives.

RW-BOSS-black-knife-assassin-4.text: A group of assassins who were responsible for the murder of Godwyn the Golden on the Night of Black Knives, using blades imbued with the power of death in a ritual performed by Ranni the Witch. They used Concealing Veils to hide their presence, rendering them effectively invisible.

RW-BOSS-ancient-hero-of-zamor.text: A clan of knights who reside in the Mountaintops of the Giants, who earned renown during the war against the Fire Giants, their mortal enemies. They hail from the town of Zamor, and cloak themselves in icy tempests. They appear as tall, slender humanoids with long, silver hair and ornate masks. They are primarily found in the Zamor Ruins in the Mountaintops of the Giants.

RW-BOSS-sanguine-noble.text: Nobles who serve Mohg, Lord of Blood. They serve as both assassins who emerge from pools of blood to strike down foes, and missionaries who share the gospel of the accursed blood. They bear elaborate designs on their shoulders to signify the noble rank they intend to claim once Mohg's dynasty has been established.

RW-BOSS-kindreds-of-rot-2x.text: Anthropomorphic, insectoid beings that emerged from the Swamp of Aeonia, they are forsaken servants and unwanted children of the new Goddess of Rot. They are commonly found in places blighted by Scarlet Rot, such as Caelid and the Grand Cloister.

RW-BOSS-magma-wyrm-2.text: Magma Wyrms are quadrupedal draconic beings with torn, vestigial wings and broad heads. They were once human heroes who partook in Dragon Communion, for which they were cursed to crawl the earth as flightless imitations of Dragons, losing their humanity in the process. They wield greatswords that resemble the jawbones of dragons, and can spew magma from their mouths.

RW-BOSS-demi-human-queen-maggie.text: A demi-human queen residing in the Hermit Village on Mt. Gelmir. She is surrounded by other demi-humans as well as Glintstone Sorcerers. She guards the resting spot of Primeval Sorcerer Azur.

RW-BOSS-red-wolf-of-the-champion.text: Giant wolves with red fur adorned with jewellery. They are agile foes, capable of casting Glintblade sorceries. Some can manifest a golden sword, which they grip with their jaws in order to perform slashing attacks.

RW-BOSS-demi-human-queen-margot.text: Demi-Human Queens tower over the average Demi-Human. They possess long, lanky limbs and canine features, and wear crowns and tattered capes. The staves they wield, which are styled as sceptres, were given to the Demi-Humans to foster peace, but are sneered at by fools at the Academy.

RW-BOSS-full-grown-fallingstar-beast.text: Fallingstar Beasts are creatures formed of shiny black rock. They have spiky tails, patches of white fur, and insect-like mandibles. They are found in craters, likely indicating that they plummeted onto the Lands Between from a great distance.

RW-BOSS-ulcerated-tree-spirit-2.text: Giant, serpentine entities with bark-like skin covered in red pustules, commonly found near the roots of the Erdtree. They use their claws and tails in combat, and can generate a burst of golden fire.

RW-BOSS-abductor-virgins-2x.text: Abductor Virgins are automatons affiliated with the Volcano Manor. Originally designed with the intent of capturing and transposing victims for interrogation, they can be found strewn around the Lands Between. Though the majority have lost their powers of transposition, they will still attempt to fulfill their original directive if approached.

RW-BOSS-godskin-noble.text: Stout humanoids who wear robes sewn together from patches of soft skin, featuring seven-faced aprons. They are the most ancient of the apostles who once served the Gloam-Eyed Queen, and they have incorporated inhuman physiology, not unlike the primordial crucible. They wield elegant thrusting swords with skill unmatched by lowborns, and wield black flame much like the Godskin Apostles.

RW-BOSS-tree-sentinels-2x.text: An order of knights, dedicated to the protection of the Erdtree. They are considered to be the living rampart of the Erdtree, and served as inspiration for Leyndell's knights.

RW-BOSS-onyx-lord-2.text: The stone-skinned Onyx Lords belonged to a race of ancients that was granted life when a meteor struck the Lands Between long ago. In contrast to the Alabaster Lords, their gravitational-based glintstone sorceries focused on repulsion and the summoning of destructive Meteorites. They were worshiped and feared of their destructive power.

RW-BOSS-bell-bearing-hunter-3.text: Elemer of the Briar, also known as the Bell Bearing Hunter, originally hailed from Eochaid, a land of proudly solitary ascetics. He wears iron armor wrapped in iron thorns, which are a mark of the guilty and of those sentenced to death. He was slated for execution at the Shaded Castle, home of the family of House Marais, however he evaded death by snatching the sword from the site of his looming execution and furnished it with battle skills from his homeland. He gained the moniker "Bell Bearing Hunter" by killing numerous merchants and instructors, and taking their Bell Bearings.

RW-BOSS-deathbird-3.text: Deathbirds are gigantic decaying birds with incrusted corpses over their body.

RW-BOSS-crucible-knights-2x.text: Ordovis was a leader of the Crucible Knights who served Lord Godfrey. He was one of the order's two most-renowned knights, and his men bore the mark of the axe.

RW-BOSS-grave-warden-duelist-2.text: Former gladiators who were exiled from the colosseum. They wear bronze armor adorned with snakes, which are viewed as traitors to the Erdtree, and as such the audiences of their duels would delight in seeing them beaten and battered.

RW-BOSS-draconic-tree-sentinel.text: Misshapen Tree Sentinels using a malformed golden armor adorned with various dragon imagery.

RW-BOSS-godfrey-first-elden-lord.text: Godfrey is regarded as the first Elden Lord of the Golden Order, and the former consort of Queen Marika the Eternal. Godfrey was once a ferocious warrior, but when he vowed to become a lord he took upon his back the lion Serosh, the Lord of Beasts, to suppress his ceaseless lust for battle.

RW-BOSS-morgott-the-omen-king.text: Morgott was born of the Golden Lineage, the offspring of the first Elden Lord, Godfrey and Queen Marika, and was the twin brother of Mohg. The twins were both born as accursed Omen, and as a result were confined to the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds below the capital. Because they were born of royalty, their horns were not excised. Unlike his brother, Morgott would renounce his accursed blood and seal it away within a warped blade of shimmering hue, which was in turn concealed within a wooden staff he carried.

RW-BOSS-fell-twins-2x.text: The Omen are accursed beings, distinguished by the advancement of their curse. Excised Omen have had their horns brutally cut, a process that not many of their babies survive. They do not harbor wraiths within, and thus must rely on more conventional combat techniques. Weak Accursed Omen, born of royalty, possess some horn growth but are forced to live underground in secrecy. They harbor some amount of wraiths, which they can expel from their mouths at foes.

RW-BOSS-esgar-priest-of-blood.text: A follower of Mohg, Lord of Blood who is encountered in the Leyndell Catacombs, hidden within the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds. Esgar wields a Reduvia and uses blood incantations. He is accompanies by two strays that inflict Blood Loss.

RW-BOSS-mohg-the-omen.text: Mohg or Mohgwyn, also known as the Lord of Blood, was born of the Golden Lineage, the offspring of the first Elden Lord, Godfrey and Queen Marika, and was the twin brother of Morgott. The twins were both born as accursed Omen, and as a result were confined and shackled to the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds below Leyndell.

RW-BOSS-night-s-cavalry-4.text: The Night's Cavalry are knights who ride atop funeral steeds and were once led by Margit, the Fell Omen, delivering death to great warriors, knights, and champions. Presently, they can be found across the Lands Between, appearing only at night, often carrying Ashes of War and equipment which can be looted upon their defeat.

RW-BOSS-black-blade-kindred.text: The Black Blade Kindred are Valiant Gargoyles who serve Maliketh, the Black Blade. These golems wield bronze weapons mended with blackened corpse wax, and are able to harness the power of the Rune of Death, with attacks that drain one's health.

RW-BOSS-ulcerated-tree-spirit-3.text: Giant, serpentine entities with bark-like skin covered in red pustules, commonly found near the roots of the Erdtree. They use their claws and tails in combat, and can generate a burst of golden fire.

RW-BOSS-rykard-lord-of-blasphemy.text: Rykard was born the son of Radagon, a champion of the Erdtree, and Queen Rennala, head of both the Carian Royal Family and the Academy of Raya Lucaria. He had two siblings, Radahn and Ranni.

RW-BOSS-erdtree-avatar.text: Beings with bodies resembling hollow tree stumps. The avatars emerged in the wake of the shattering of the Elden Ring in order to protect the Minor Erdtrees. They wield large staffs depicting the Erdtree, and are capable of utilising offensive incantations.

RW-BOSS-death-rite-bird-3.text: Death Rite Birds are gigantic decaying birds with incrusted corpses over their body, partially covered in ghostflame and guarded by the spirits of the servants of death inside their wings.

RW-BOSS-commander-niall.text: Commander Niall, a veteran general of Castle Sol, offered his prosthesis in exchange for the lives of imprisoned knights, forming an army of no nation. A lone survivor, Nial commands the spirits of deceased knights to defend his long-passed master.

RW-BOSS-borealis-the-freezing-fog.text: Weaker descendants of the Ancient Dragons who once ruled the Lands Between. They did not inherit their ancestors' stone scales nor their command over lightning and so are vulnerable to it, and the very Gravelstone scales posessed by the ancient dragons can cause them mortal harm.

RW-BOSS-spiritcaller-snail-2.text: Pale, serpentine snails possessing the ability to summon spirits by emitting a ringing sound, akin to a Spirit Calling Bell. They possess limited offensive capabilities of their own, relying on their spirits to protect them. In some cases, they can teleport or turn themselves invisible.

RW-BOSS-roundtable-knight-vyke.text: Vyke was a Tarnished champion better known for being the closest to becoming Elden Lord before the arrival of the player protagonist.

RW-BOSS-ancient-hero-of-zamor-2.text: A clan of knights who reside in the Mountaintops of the Giants, who earned renown during the war against the Fire Giants, their mortal enemies. They hail from the town of Zamor, and cloak themselves in icy tempests. They appear as tall, slender humanoids with long, silver hair and ornate masks. They are primarily found in the Zamor Ruins in the Mountaintops of the Giants.

RW-BOSS-fire-giant.text: In the days before the Erdtree, the Giants carved out a civilization in the inhospitable mountains to the north, after chasing away the Ice Dragons who had previously ruled it. Here, they worshipped a Fell God and were bound to tend the Flame of their god for eternity.

RW-BOSS-black-blade-kindred-2.text: The Black Blade Kindred are Valiant Gargoyles who serve Maliketh, the Black Blade. These golems wield bronze weapons mended with blackened corpse wax, and are able to harness the power of the Rune of Death, with attacks that drain one's health.

RW-BOSS-flying-dragon-greyll.text: Weaker descendants of the Ancient Dragons who once ruled the Lands Between. They did not inherit their ancestors' stone scales nor their command over lightning and so are vulnerable to it, and the very Gravelstone scales posessed by the ancient dragons can cause them mortal harm.

RW-BOSS-putrid-avatar-2.text: Beings with bodies resembling hollow tree stumps. The avatars emerged in the wake of the shattering of the Elden Ring in order to protect the Minor Erdtrees. They wield large staffs depicting the Erdtree, and are capable of utilising offensive incantations.

RW-BOSS-night-s-cavalry-5.text: The Night's Cavalry are knights who ride atop funeral steeds and were once led by Margit, the Fell Omen, delivering death to great warriors, knights, and champions. Presently, they can be found across the Lands Between, appearing only at night, often carrying Ashes of War and equipment which can be looted upon their defeat.

RW-BOSS-beastmen-of-farum-azula-2x.text: Two Beastmen encountered in the Dragonbarrow Cave in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. One fights from range, making use of paired throwing knives, while the other uses a large cleaver.

RW-BOSS-putrid-tree-spirit.text: Giant, serpentine entities with bark-like skin covered in red pustules, commonly found near the roots of the Erdtree. They use their claws and tails in combat, and can generate a burst of golden fire.

RW-BOSS-godskin-apostle-2.text: Lanky humanoids clad in robes sewn together from patches of smooth skin. The Godskin Apostles were led by the Gloam-Eyed Queen, who cradled them as newborns in a swaddling cloth made from skin much like their robes. They served Destined Death, and wielded god-slaying black flame. However, when Maliketh, the Black Blade, sealed away the Rune of Death, the flame's true power was lost.

RW-BOSS-bell-bearing-hunter-4.text: Elemer of the Briar, also known as the Bell Bearing Hunter, originally hailed from Eochaid, a land of proudly solitary ascetics. He wears iron armor wrapped in iron thorns, which are a mark of the guilty and of those sentenced to death. He was slated for execution at the Shaded Castle, home of the family of House Marais, however he evaded death by snatching the sword from the site of his looming execution and furnished it with battle skills from his homeland. He gained the moniker "Bell Bearing Hunter" by killing numerous merchants and instructors, and taking their Bell Bearings.

RW-BOSS-stray-mimic-tear.text: Formless creatures of mimicry found in and around the Eternal Cities. They make a mockery of life, reborn again and again into imitation. They are viscous, silver droplets, and they can manifest spear-like appendages from their bodies. Some can generate electricity, while others sport hardened shields that protect them from damage.

RW-BOSS-putrid-grave-warden-duelist.text: Former gladiators who were exiled from the colosseum. They wear bronze armor adorned with snakes, which are viewed as traitors to the Erdtree, and as such the audiences of their duels would delight in seeing them beaten and battered.

RW-BOSS-putrid-avatar-3.text: Beings with bodies resembling hollow tree stumps. The avatars emerged in the wake of the shattering of the Elden Ring in order to protect the Minor Erdtrees. They wield large staffs depicting the Erdtree, and are capable of utilising offensive incantations.

RW-BOSS-misbegotten-crusader.text: Hulking Misbegotten with long, red manes and serpentine tails. Misbegotten Warriors typically fight using large, iron greatswords. As with other Misbegotten, their appearance is seen as a punishment for making contact with the Primordial Crucible.

RW-BOSS-great-wyrm-theodorix.text: Magma Wyrms are quadrupedal draconic beings with torn, vestigial wings and broad heads. They were once human heroes who partook in Dragon Communion, for which they were cursed to crawl the earth as flightless imitations of Dragons, losing their humanity in the process. They wield greatswords that resemble the jawbones of dragons, and can spew magma from their mouths.

RW-BOSS-night-s-cavalries-2x.text: The Night's Cavalry are knights who ride atop funeral steeds and were once led by Margit, the Fell Omen, delivering death to great warriors, knights, and champions. Presently, they can be found across the Lands Between, appearing only at night, often carrying Ashes of War and equipment which can be looted upon their defeat.

RW-BOSS-astel-stars-of-darkness.text: A malformed star born in a flightless void far away, composed of many-colored star debris. It is said to have assailed an Eternal City, destroying it and taking away its sky.

RW-BOSS-death-rite-bird-4.text: Death Rite Birds are gigantic decaying birds with incrusted corpses over their body, partially covered in ghostflame and guarded by the spirits of the servants of death inside their wings.

RW-BOSS-mohg-lord-of-blood.text: Mohg or Mohgwyn, also known as the Lord of Blood, was born of the Golden Lineage, the offspring of the first Elden Lord, Godfrey and Queen Marika, and was the twin brother of Morgott. The twins were both born as accursed Omen, and as a result were confined and shackled to the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds below Leyndell.

RW-BOSS-loretta-knight-of-the-haligtree.text: Loretta was once a royal Carian knight, and served as a personal guard for Carian royalty. Loretta's favored weapon was said to be the bow, and she developed sorceries imitating the power of a greatbow.

RW-BOSS-malenia-blade-of-miquella.text: Malenia was born the child of Queen Marika the Eternal and her second husband, the Elden Lord Radagon. She had an elder twin brother by the name of Miquella. Both Malenia and Miquella were Empyreans, meaning they had the potential to one day replace their mother as a new god of a coming age. But since Radagon and Marika were in fact the same person, Malenia and Miquella were born afflicted. Malenia was afflicted with the Scarlet Rot, which ravaged her from within and would cost her several limbs, while Miquella was afflicted with eternal childhood, unable to ever grow into adulthood.

RW-BOSS-godskin-duo.text: Godskin Duo is a boss battle where you have to battle against a Godskin Apostle and Godskin Noble at the same time. They can be found in Crumbling Farum Azula. This is not an optional boss as they must be defeated to advance further in Crumbling Farum Azula.

RW-BOSS-dragonlord-placidusax.text: In the prehistoric era before the age of the Erdtree, the world was ruled by the Ancient Dragons. Above them all was Placidusax, a many-headed Ancient Dragon who ruled as Elden Lord from the royal city of Farum Azula.

RW-BOSS-maliketh-the-black-blade.text: Maliketh is the loyal Shadowbound Beast and half-brother of Queen Marika the Eternal, an Empyrean of Numen descent, who would become the vessel of the Elden Ring.

RW-BOSS-sir-gideon-ofnir-the-all-knowing.text: Gideon Ofnir is the Tarnished leader of Roundtable Hold and the adoptive father of Nepheli Loux. Called to the Lands Between by the guidance of Grace, Gideon wishes to become Elden Lord. To this end he accumulates information on the Shardbearers, employing a network of spies to aid in his hunt for knowledge. Initially, he is apprehensive of the Tarnished, but after they have claimed a Great Rune he becomes willing to share his knowledge of the remaining shardbearers.

RW-BOSS-godfrey-first-elden-lord-2.text: Godfrey is regarded as the first Elden Lord of the Golden Order, and the former consort of Queen Marika the Eternal. Godfrey was once a ferocious warrior, but when he vowed to become a lord he took upon his back the lion Serosh, the Lord of Beasts, to suppress his ceaseless lust for battle.

RW-BOSS-radagon-of-the-golden-order-and-.text: Radagon first rose to prominence during the Liurnian Wars, when he joined the heroes' ranks. A great champion with flowing red locks, he arrived in Liurnia at the head of a golden host, where he met Queen Rennala in battle. Although two wars would be fought between them, the First Liurnian War, and the Second, no victor would emerge from either. Radagon eventually repented his territorial aggressions by cleansing himself with Celestial Dew, and swore his love to Rennala. He became husband to the Carian Queen, wedding her at the Church of Vows.

RW-BOSS-knight-of-the-solitary-gaol.text: The nameless spirit of a member of the Knights of the Solitary Gaol that lingers within a mausoleum in the Realm of Shadow. These knights offered their hearts through esoteric rite, gaining heightened battle prowess. Their steel greatswords bear two carved emblems: one symbolizing the light of birth and the other, solitude.

RW-BOSS-ghostflame-dragon.text: The ghostflame dragons were the rotting remains of dragons that drifted into the Realm of Shadow. They clung so tenaciously to life that they became Those Who Live in Death.

RW-BOSS-demi-human-swordmaster-onze.text: In a bygone era, when beasts were granted intelligence, the demi-human swordsmen were bequeathed Star-Lined Swords by their queens. Their royal blades were encrusted with shards of crude glintstone, symbolizing the procession of the stars. Each swordsman swore an oath to unveil the secret that awaited at the end of the line of stars.

RW-BOSS-death-knight.text: These knights were once the personal guard of Godwyn, and are now the protectors of the Prince of Death's cadaver surrogate.

RW-BOSS-ancient-dragon-man.text: Formerly a Dragon Communion warrior, the Ancient Dragon-Man was once arbiter of those worthy to devour the Dreaded One.

RW-BOSS-chief-bloodfiend.text: Long ago, a subjugated tribe discovered a twisted deity amongst the ravages of war, and they were transformed into bloodfiends. The mother of truth was their savior, and this is their chief.

RW-BOSS-divine-beast-dancing-lion.text: The divine beasts were messengers of the heavens. The sculpted keepers are representations used to perform the ritual of the lion dance during the tower festival in Belurat, Tower Settlement. Only the greatest of horned warriors became divine beast warriors, and few became sculpted keepers.

RW-BOSS-demi-human-queen-marigga.text: Drops the Star-Lined Sword, which implies she bestowed this weapon to the Demi-human swordsmen who swore to find the truth that lies at the end of the procession of stars.

RW-BOSS-dancer-of-ranah.text: The Dancer of Ranah is located in the Southern Nameless Mausoleum located on the Cerulean Coast. It lies on an island in the sea and the Tarnished needs to cross a cave to reach her.

RW-BOSS-ghostflame-dragon-2.text: The ghostflame dragons were the rotting remains of dragons that drifted into the Realm of Shadow. They clung so tenaciously to life that they became Those Who Live in Death.

RW-BOSS-death-rite-bird-5.text: Death Rite Birds are gigantic decaying birds with incrusted corpses over their body, partially covered in ghostflame and guarded by the spirits of the servants of death inside their wings.

RW-BOSS-lamenter.text: The state of a denizen of paradise. The people of the tower denied and hid it from the world. In their foolishness, they viewed true bliss with deep fear. <!--

RW-BOSS-rellana-twin-moon-knight.text: Born as a princess into the Carian Royal Family, Rellana is the younger sister of Rennala, who gifted her lustrous black hair . In her childhood, she and her elder sister met the twin moon, which were overlapping, as though nestled against one another . Rellana also had a sole entry into ritual combat—a demonstration of fidelity to the Erdtree .

RW-BOSS-black-knight-garrew.text: The Black Knights are an order of knights who are devoted servants of Messmer the Impaler, serving as the primary force in his army. They were under the command of their first leader Black Knight Commander Andreas, a man of great strength who has command over the primordial powers of the Crucible. Having absolute loyalty to their master, the Black Knights possess an iron conviction to their Crusade, and they never yield nor doubt their purpose. Although the crest on their armour is a Scadutree design, it is etched in gold, as a consolation for those forced to wage a war without grace or honor.

RW-BOSS-ralva-the-great-red-bear.text: Giant bears found throughout the Lands Between and Realm of Shadow. They are far larger than other Bears, and display strange markings on their chests.

RW-BOSS-dryleaf-dane.text: Dane is a member of the Dryleaf Sect, an order of spiritual seekers who chose to serve a new god after seeing the decline of the Erdtree in the fallen leaves. Dane fights using an unarmed technique which focuses on kicks.

RW-BOSS-ghostflame-dragon-3.text: The ghostflame dragons were the rotting remains of dragons that drifted into the Realm of Shadow. They clung so tenaciously to life that they became Those Who Live in Death.

RW-BOSS-black-knight-edredd.text: The Black Knights are an order of knights who are devoted servants of Messmer the Impaler, serving as the primary force in his army. They were under the command of their first leader Black Knight Commander Andreas, a man of great strength who has command over the primordial powers of the Crucible. Having absolute loyalty to their master, the Black Knights possess an iron conviction to their Crusade, and they never yield nor doubt their purpose. Although the crest on their armour is a Scadutree design, it is etched in gold, as a consolation for those forced to wage a war without grace or honor.

RW-BOSS-curseblade-labirith.text: Curseblades appear to dance when they spin their shimmering circular blades. These ascetics, who failed to become tutelary deities, were a scourge for those who attempted to invade the hornsent homeland.

RW-BOSS-red-bear.text: Red Bear is a former Redmane soldier whose true name has been lost to madness. After killing a great red bear in a bloody bout, he became fascinated with the beast's untainted naked strength and took its claw and used it as a weapon without any modifications. It was at that point that Red Bear decided that he wanted to become a bear himself, no more, and no less. He channels the power of Rugalea the Great Red Bear to temporary transform himself into a great read bear and unleashes a mighty roar, for only through a desperate battle with the untamed wild can one discover a god unique to oneself.

RW-BOSS-rugalea-the-great-red-bear.text: Giant bears found throughout the Lands Between and Realm of Shadow. They are far larger than other Bears, and display strange markings on their chests.

RW-BOSS-death-knight-2.text: These knights were once the personal guard of Godwyn, and are now the protectors of the Prince of Death's cadaver surrogate.

RW-BOSS-putrescent-knight.text: The Putrescent Knight was a mass of putrid flesh that imbibed the nectar of St. Trina, transforming it into a knight dedicated to St. Trina's service.

RW-BOSS-golden-hippopotamus.text: Hippopotami are giant quadrupeds that live near bodies of water. Several can be found in the Realm of Shadow. One particular specimen in the Shadow Keep, called the Golden Hippopotamus, can grow thorn-like fur on its back; a vestige of the vitality of the Crucible which flourished before the land was enshrouded in shadow.

RW-BOSS-scadutree-avatar.text: The Scadutree Avatar is the guardian of the Scadutree, as well as the holder of Miquella's Great Rune after Miquella of the Haligtree discarded it.

RW-BOSS-commander-gaius.text: Gaius was a commander in the army of Messmer the Impaler, and an Albinauric who relied upon a boar mount to compensate for his missing legs. Gaius was a friend to Messmer, as well as both an elder brotherly figure and rival of Radahn. He was also the most senior disciple of the same Alabaster Lord who taught Radahn his gravitational techniques.

RW-BOSS-messmer-the-impaler.text: Messmer was a son of Queen Marika the Eternal. He was born with a dark serpent inside him that threatened to subsume him, which Messmer has called the Abyssal Serpent; Marika was able to contain its influence by removing one of Messmer's eyes and replacing it with a seal of grace. Ever since his accursed birth, Messmer was in constant company of the winged serpents.

RW-BOSS-tree-sentinel.text: An order of knights, dedicated to the protection of the Erdtree. They are considered to be the living rampart of the Erdtree, and served as inspiration for Leyndell's knights.

RW-BOSS-tree-sentinel-2.text: An order of knights, dedicated to the protection of the Erdtree. They are considered to be the living rampart of the Erdtree, and served as inspiration for Leyndell's knights.

RW-BOSS-fallingstar-beast-3.text: Fallingstar Beasts are creatures formed of shiny black rock. They have spiky tails, patches of white fur, and insect-like mandibles. They are found in craters, likely indicating that they plummeted onto the Lands Between from a great distance.

RW-BOSS-metyr-mother-of-fingers.text: Metyr, brilliant daughter of the Greater Will, was the first of all stars to fall upon the Lands Between. She possessed a microcosm which allowed her to receive messages from the Greater Will. Metyr gave birth to the Two Fingers that guide the empyreans and the Tarnished.

RW-BOSS-count-ymir-mother-of-fingers.text: Ymir is a glintstone sorcerer who resides in the Cathedral of Manus Metyr. Ymir once instructed Rellana, a princess of the Carian Royal Family, however he abandoned his alliegence to the moon, believing it to be merely the closest of the celestial bodies. He is served by Jolán, Swordhand of Night, who is fiercely loyal to her count.

RW-BOSS-rakshasa.text: Rakshasa is located in the Eastern Nameless Mausoleum, within the Recluses' River area of Scadu Altus. The Mausoleum is located near a river bank.

RW-BOSS-jori-elder-inquisitor.text: One of the hornsent inquisitors, who are tasked with torture and questioning.

RW-BOSS-midra-lord-of-frenzied-flame.text: Long ago, the great Sage Midra attempted to become a Lord of Frenzied Flame. However, he was too weak and failed. Pierced by the branching thorns of the Greatsword of Damnation, his power was suppressed by the hornsent. Midra's Manse and the dark lands of the Abyssal Woods were forbidden by the Hornsent. It is said the eyes of those who served the sage were burned by the Frenzied Flame of madness. Midra lingered on in perpetual suffering at the behest of his beloved Nanaya.

RW-BOSS-jagged-peak-drake-bottom.text: Weaker descendants of the Ancient Dragons who once ruled the Lands Between. They did not inherit their ancestors' stone scales nor their command over lightning and so are vulnerable to it, and the very Gravelstone scales posessed by the ancient dragons can cause them mortal harm.

RW-BOSS-jagged-peak-drake.text: Weaker descendants of the Ancient Dragons who once ruled the Lands Between. They did not inherit their ancestors' stone scales nor their command over lightning and so are vulnerable to it, and the very Gravelstone scales posessed by the ancient dragons can cause them mortal harm.

RW-BOSS-ancient-dragon-senessax.text: Ancient Dragons have light grey bodies resembling stone. They possess four legs, as well as four wings inlayed with gold, distinguishing them from their lesser descendants. They have short, flat muzzles, orange-yellow eyes, and wispy grey hairs along their backs. They can breathe fire like many of their descendants, however they also possess the ability to wield red lightning, which often manifests in the form of spears and glaives.

RW-BOSS-bayle-the-dread.text: Bayle the Dread was a legendary black dragon who is said to be the ancestor of the drakes or lesser dragons. Long ago, Bayle betrayed the Ancient dragons and clashed with Dragonlord Placidusax. Their vicious battle ended in stalemate and left both dragons with grievous injuries and loss of body parts, with Bayle losing his two winged arms, his pair of wings on his back and his left leg, with the dreaded dragon fleeing to the Jagged Peak soon afterwards.

RW-BOSS-divine-beast-dancing-lion-2.text: The divine beasts were messengers of the heavens. The sculpted keepers are representations used to perform the ritual of the lion dance during the tower festival in Belurat, Tower Settlement. Only the greatest of horned warriors became divine beast warriors, and few became sculpted keepers.

RW-BOSS-romina-saint-of-the-bud.text: Romina is one of the many victims of Messmer the Impaler's crusade throughout the Realm of Shadow, with her church being burned to the ground. In the crumbling, burning church, Romina held the bud in speechless silence.

RW-BOSS-promised-consort-radahn.text: Following Radahn's defeat, his soul met its end. However, Miquella sought to revive it, still desiring for Radahn to be his lord consort. Miquella was successful in reviving Radahn, placing his soul into a vessel made from the remains of Mohg, Lord of Blood, another Demigod slain by the same Tarnished who had defeated Radahn. The Tarnished encounters the newly-resurrected Radahn at the Gate of Divinity at the top of Enir-Ilim. Radahn stands guard as Miquella completes his ascension to godhood and battles the Tarnished once more.

TP-ENC-LEONTIEL.text: Leontiel comes from a proud order of orthodox knights that existed long ago. The mask that is affixed to her ceremonial hat is modeled after Witch-Hunter Jerren, who she saw as a father figure of sorts.

TP-ENC-BROKEN-GOLD-MASK.text:
A mask designed to resemble a blazing golden halo, though a piece is now broken off.

The attire of the honorable Goldmask's closest disciple, and dear friend, who accompanied him on his great venture. Enhances incantations and skills that harness Causality.

Upon the splintering of the Golden Order, so too did these companions part ways. One kept the faith, though the faith itself was broken, while the other fell completely to his own doubts.

Alexander, Warrior Jar.text: Alexander is a living jar who travels the Lands Between, honing his strength in order to become a great warrior. Alexander was created to be a warrior vessel, and the remains of many great warriors reside within him. He originally came from Jarburg, a hidden village of living jars in Liurnia of the Lakes, however he vowed never to return, claiming that "the path of champions must be trod alone".

Blackguard Big Boggart.text: Boggart is an ex-convict who was called to the Lands Between by the Guidance of Grace. At some point in the past he was imprisoned in the same gaol as the Dung Eater, and saw first hand the ways he defiles and kills people.

Blaidd the Half-Wolf.text: Blaidd was created by Ranni's own Two Fingers as a vassal to Lunar Princess Ranni and to be incapable of treachery towards her, as she was one of the three Empyreans candidates chosen by the Greater Will, along with Miquella and Malenia, to eventually replace their mother Queen Marika the Eternal as the God of a new age.

Boc the Seamster.text: Boc the Seamster or Demi-Human Boc is an NPC in Elden Ring. He offers the player the ability to modify their garments, free of charge.

Brother Corhyn.text: Brother Corhyn is a cleric of the Golden Order, who was granted the guidance of Grace due to his iron will and unwavering faith in the face of his exile. At some point, Corhyn made his way to Roundtable Hold, where he teaches the incantations of the Two Fingers to Tarnished of the Roundtable, hoping that one of them might one day claim the title of Elden Lord, so that Corhyn might council them. When a Tarnished champion makes their way to the Roundtable, Corhyn introduces himself to them, and offers his tutelage.

Count Ymir, High Priest.text: Ymir is a glintstone sorcerer who resides in the Cathedral of Manus Metyr. Ymir once instructed Rellana, a princess of the Carian Royal Family, however he abandoned his alliegence to the moon, believing it to be merely the closest of the celestial bodies. He is served by Jolán, Swordhand of Night, who is fiercely loyal to her count.

D, Beholder of Death.text: Devin, more commonly known as "D", is the twin-brother of Darian, who is also known as D. The two twins had separate minds and bodies, but shared a single soul. For this, they were reviled as accursed beings, but found solace in the Golden Order, which accepted them both.

D, Hunter of the Dead.text: Darian, more commonly known as D, Hunter of the Dead is an undead hunter and an ally of Gurranq, the Beast Clergyman. Darian has a twin brother by the name of Devin, who was also called D. While Darien and Devin had different minds and bodies, they shared a single soul, and were reviled as cursed beings. The twins found sanctuary in the Golden Order, the only institution to accept them.

Dryleaf Dane.text: Dane is a member of the Dryleaf Sect, an order of spiritual seekers who chose to serve a new god after seeing the decline of the Erdtree in the fallen leaves. Dane fights using an unarmed technique which focuses on kicks.

Dung Eater.text: The Dung Eater once saw guidance and a ring that would appear at the end of his journey. His vision is of a curse he calls the "pox upon life itself" or the "reviled blessing", with everyone sustaining it in despair and their souls not being able to return to the Erdtree. He decided to wear a disfigured armor, resembling the Omen, representing the vision of the landscape of his mind, and his appearance as he wished to see it. He donned his armor with a heavy sun-shaped medallion to represent both the guidance and the ring he once saw.

Ensha of the Royal Remains.text: Ensha is the unspeaking adherent of Sir Gideon Ofnir, typically found leaning on the wall outside his master's study in Roundtable Hold. Ensha wears armour graced with golden human bones, which are said to have belonged to a soulless king, the lord of the lost and desperate, known as Ensha.

Fia, Deathbed Companion.text: Fia was once a Deathbed Companion. She would receive the warmth and vigor from champions, and then lay with the remains of an exalted noble, to grant him another chance at life. This was the sole purpose of Fia's existence, and was considered a sacred act in her homeland.

Finger Reader Enia.text: Enia is a Finger Reader, much like the Finger Reader Crones scattered across the Lands Between. She interprets the words of the Two Fingers, envoys of the Greater Will. The Tarnished meets her in the Two Fingers' audience chamber in Roundtable Hold after claiming a Great Rune, where she imparts the wisdom of the Two Fingers upon them, revealing that they must gather more Great Runes to repair the shattered Elden Ring and become Elden Lord. In addition to her guidance, Enia offers to grant the Tarnished the power housed within the Remembrances they gain from killing powerful foes.

Fire Knight Queelign.text:
Ashen remains in which spirits yet dwell. Use to summon the spirit of Fire Knight Queelign. Attacks immediately after being summoned.

Spirit of a knight granted relief by the Iris of Grace. Wields a spear-like greatsword that impales foes upon fire, keeping the taint of impurity away from fair mother Marika.

That grace was his salvation, though it was but a fleeting blessing. And having been saved, all that was left to him was to wage war.

Florissax, Dragon Communion Priestess.text: Florissax is an Ancient Dragon who assumed a human form to share Dragon Comunion with the world. A loyal servant of Dragonlord Placidusax, Florissax offers her sleep to her lord each night, to receive his blessing in turn. She seeks to aid in the destruction of Bayle the Dread, a Dragon who turned on Placidusax and inflicted a grievous wound upon him long ago.

Gatekeeper Gostoc.text: Gostoc is a servant working in Stormveil Castle, in the role of gatekeeper. Gostoc detests his master, Godrick the Grafted, who always looked down on and mistreated him. Gostoc prowls the castle, looting from the corpses of the Tarnished who die in their hunt for Godrick. When he encounters the Tarnished, he offers to signal the gates to open for them, but also suggests a hidden path around the outer wall of the castle which will allow the Tarnished to get in undetected.

Gurranq, Beast Clergyman.text: Gurranq is a hulking, bestial clergyman who resides in the Bestial Sanctum in north-eastern Caelid. Long ago, his terrifying ferocity earned him the name "Death of the Demigods. Presently, he seeks Deathroot, a product of the Rune of Death which spread through the Lands Between following the murder of Godwyn the Golden on the Night of Black Knives. Gurranq consumes Deathroot, although it does not appear to sate him.

Hornsent.text: At first glance, Hornsent seems a living contradiction. When you meet him, he bluntly scorns the Tarnished and their loyalty to the Erdtree, and yet, he helps you find places where Miquella left behind parts of his being. Is there more to his motives for cooperation? Like Freyja, you can find Hornsent at the Three-Path Cross Site of Grace on the Gravesite Plains.

Hornsent Grandam.text: An old hornsent bitter with resentment towards Marika, Messmer, and any of their ilk, since during the Crusade many hornsent perished, their lands were burnt, and their tower veiled in shadow. Many of them used to live at tower settlement of Belurat, where she can still be found.

Igon.text: Igon was once a poor scavenger of battlefields, but found honour in the ancient art of Dragon Communion, whereby hunters of dragons could consume their hearts to gain their strength.

Irina of Morne.text: Irina is the daughter of Edgar, castellan of Castle Morne. Her eyesight has been weak since birth, and she wears a blindfold around her eyes.

Jar-Bairn.text: Jar-Bairn is a young Living Jar who lives in the secluded village of Jarburg in Liurnia of the Lakes. Like his uncle Alexander, he is a warrior jar, and strives to become a champion just like Alexander.

Kenneth Haight.text: Kenneth Haight is a nobleman and claims to be next in line as the rightful ruler of Limgrave. He resided in a fort known as Fort Haight, and is known for his considerable largesse, at least by his own account. Godrick the Grafted assumed control of Limgrave following the Shattering, and at some point sent a knight commander to seize Fort Haight.

Knight Bernahl.text: Residing in the Warmaster's Shack of Limgrave, Knight Bernahl (騎士ベルナール) is a tarnished merchant who sells a number of Ashes of War. Bernahl was once a Tarnished champion worthy of becoming a lord, until his Finger Maiden cast herself into the flames.

Knight Diallos.text: Diallos Hoslow is a scion of House Hoslow and the younger brother of Juno Hoslow. From a young age, Diallos was all talk and no trousers, with an inability to commit to action. As a result, Juno inherited the Hoslow legacy without resistance. Juno loved his brother dearly and showered him with adoration. Diallos, in turn, admired his brother, a mighty warrior who lived up to the bloody legacy of House Hoslow. Diallos aspired to be like his older brother, knowing that pursuing the bloody legacy of their house would break his brother's heart.

Latenna the Albinauric.text: Latenna is an Albinauric woman and a deft archer. Latenna and her wolf companion Lobo began their journey in the lands of the Haligtree, a sanctuary for Albinaurics. She journeyed to the far south, eventually coming to Liurnia of the Lakes.

Lightseeker Hyetta.text: Hyetta is a blind woman travelling alone through the Lands Between, following a distant light which she believes will lead her to her duty as a Finger Maiden. To this end, she asks for donations of Shabriri Grapes, which allow her to see the light in the back of her eyes.

Melina.text: Melina was born at the foot of the Erdtree and describes her mother as within the Erdtree. Although it is never stated, it can be inferred that her mother is Queen Marika the Eternal. During Boc's questline she asks if "being born of a mother" means acting in certain ways, which makes the specifics of her origins unclear.

Millicent.text: Millicent is a red-haired woman afflicted by Scarlet Rot. She and her sisters were found in the Swamp of Aeonia in Caelid by Sage Gowry, who raised them as his daughters. Her four sisters travelled to Miquella's Haligtree under Gowry's guidance, however Millicent alone remained behind.

Moore.text: Moore was once a pest who awaited the return of the goddess of the Scarlet Rot. When her successor, Malenia, disowned and abandoned the pests, Moore and his forager brood were left without a master. He and his kin later allied with Miquella and joined his followers. The brood shared their scavenged items with Moore and his comrades out of kindness.

Needle Knight Leda.text: A member of the Needle Knights, an order devoted to Miquella of the Haligtree. Leda was guided by Miquella to the Realm of Shadow alongside her compatriots, all of whom were under the influence of a powerful charm which compelled them to follow the Empyrean. While in the Realm of Shadow, Leda followed the trail of crosses left by Miquella, discovering in the process that he sought the Gate of Divinity, which was sealed away by a tree.

Nepheli Loux.text: Nepheli Loux is a Tarnished warrior from the Badlands. In her infancy, Nepheli lived through murder and pillage unchecked At some point, she lost the guidance of grace, and was taken in by Gideon Ofnir, who became her foster father. Gideon promised Nepheli that if he became Elden Lord he would never allow the downtrodden to be cheated again, earning her loyalty and aid in his pursuit of the title of Elden Lord.

Patches.text: A Tarnished who leads a group of bandits, operating out of Murkwater Cave in Limgrave. Patches is a nomadic and free-spirited individual with a proclivity for tricking people and robbing them of their possessions.

Preceptor Seluvis.text: A preceptor in the service of Ranni the Witch, the last princess of the Carian Royal Family. Seluvis, who resides within a rise in the Three Sisters, openly expresses disdain towards the Tarnished speaking to them with an air of superiority and hostility.

Ranni the Witch.text: Originally known as Lunar Princess Ranni, she was the daughter of Radagon, a champion of the Golden Order, and Queen Rennala, head of both the Carian Royal Family and the Academy of Raya Lucaria. She had two older brothers, Radahn and Rykard.

Redmane Freyja.text: Formerly one of the most distinguished knights of Starscourge Radahn, who invited her into his ranks after witnessing her valour as a gladiator, Freyja is one of the compatriots of Needle Knight Leda who followed Miquella into the Realm of Shadow.

Roderika, Spirit Tuner.text: A Tarnished noblewoman who, despite having never seen the guidance of grace, travelled to the Lands Between along with her companions. After arriving, those companions fell victim to Godrick, becoming subjects for his grafting. Roderika alone survived, taking refuge in Stormhill Shack. It is here that she meets the Tarnished. She beseeches the Tarnished to bring a message to her grafted companions, whom she refers to as chrysalids, assuring them that she loves them and will join them soon.

Rya the Scout.text: A young woman who works as a scout for the Recusants of Volcano Manor, tasked with recruiting Tarnished to the cause. Rya is the adopted daughter of Tanith, although she believes her to be her true mother. In truth, Rya is a Man-Serpent of Mt. Gelmir, born of a repellent birthing ritual, and her true name is Zorayas.

Sage Gowry.text: Gowry is an elderly sage dwelling in the blighted Caelid Wilds. When the Empyrean Malenia unleashed the Scarlet Rot during her battle with General Radahn, she permanently blighted Caelid. Since that day, Gowry has dedicated himself to her and the Order of Rot he hopes she will usher in.

Sir Ansbach.text: Formerly the feared commander of the Pureblood Knights in service of Lord Mohg, Ansbach is one of the compatriots of Needle Knight Leda who followed Miquella into the Realm of Shadow. Ansbach has dedicated himself to investigating Miquella's purpose by following the trail of crosses he left behind.

Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing.text: Gideon Ofnir is the Tarnished leader of Roundtable Hold and the adoptive father of Nepheli Loux. Called to the Lands Between by the guidance of Grace, Gideon wishes to become Elden Lord. To this end he accumulates information on the Shardbearers, employing a network of spies to aid in his hunt for knowledge. Initially, he is apprehensive of the Tarnished, but after they have claimed a Great Rune he becomes willing to share his knowledge of the remaining shardbearers.

Smithing Master Hewg.text: Hewg is a prisoner of Roundtable Hold, tasked with smithing weapons for the Tarnished. His duty, given by Queen Marika the Eternal, is to smith a weapon to kill a god. In the past, Hewg was indebted to a spirit tuner, and when he meets Roderika he recognises that her eyes share the same hue as those of his old acquaintance. Although reluctant at first, Hewg agrees to take Roderika under his wing at the insistence of the Tarnished.

Sorcerer Rogier.text: Rogier is a sorcerer, who is first encountered as an optional summon against Margit, the Fell Omen, he is later found within a church searching for knowledge in Stormveil Castle. He offers to teach the Tarnished his magical combat arts and warns them about Godrick's Tarnished hunters.

Sorcerer Thops.text: A former student of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, Thops was considered a "bluntstone", lacking any talent for sorcery, yet he looked up to Sorceress Sellen prior to her expulsion from the Academy.

Sorceress Sellen.text: Sellen was considered to be the most promising glintstone sorceress to ever attend the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Her first teacher at the was the sorcerer Azur, one of the founding glintstone sorcerers and originator of the Karolos Conspectus. Azur, along with Lusat, was banished from the academy due to their study of the primeval current, a study Sellen wished to pursue. However, following accusations of unspeakable treatment of her fellow scholars under the name of the Graven Witch, Sellen too was expelled from the academy.

Swordhand of Night Jolan.text:
Ashen remains in which spirits yet dwell. Use to summon the spirit of Swordhand of Night Jolán.

Spirit of a swordhand granted light by the Iris of Grace. Wields a sword of bottomless black that penetrates the enemy's guard.

Though it was not by the shining star that she had longed for, thus was her Night illuminated. But this was an at times blinding light, and threatened to expunge the Night entirely.

Tanith, Volcano Manor Proprietress.text: Tanith is the consort of Praetor Rykard and the leader of the Recusants, a band of Tarnished who have taken up arms against the Erdtree and vowed to hunt down their own kind.

Thiollier.text: This isolated young man once met St. Trina and, just once, Thiollier was granted the sweet repose of velvety sleep. The remainder of his days would be spent attempting to recapture it.

War Counselor Iji.text: A good-natured troll who once served the Carian Royal Family as a blacksmith. Currently, Iji serves Ranni, the Carian princess, as her war counsellor, while still plying his trade as a blacksmith outside the Kingsrealm Ruins, near the Caria Manor.

White Mask Varre.text: Varré is an enigmatic man who dresses in the garb of a war surgeon. War Surgeons, despite their name, are not surgeons or doctors. They act as mercy killers on battlefields, putting dying soldiers out of their misery as quickly as possible by delivering final blows. Varré was a war surgeon prior to his association with Mohg.

Witch-Hunter Jerren.text: Jerren is the elderly castellan of Redmane Castle. In the past, Jerren was a nomadic warrior who became a guest of the Carian Royal Family. There, he became acquainted with General Radahn, the son of Radagon and Rennala, the Carian queen, who would later challenge the stars and arrest their movements, halting fate. He was considered an eccentric by Iji, the blacksmith and war counselor of the Carians. During this time, Jerren made a promise to kill Sellen, a sorceress who had long been a hindrance to the Carians.

Yura, Hunter of Bloody Fingers.text: Yura is a warrior who dresses in the garb reminiscent of that worn in the Land of Reeds. He is a self-proclaimed hunter of Bloody Fingers and a prior associate of Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger, whom he likely had strong feelings for.

Abyssal Woods.text: Below the rest of the Realm of Shadow, hidden under a sprawling canopy that blots out the light of the sky, a thick swampy woodland corrupted by Madness. Jori, the elder Hornsent Inquisitor, guards the entrance to the area at the end of the Darklight Catacombs.

Academy of Raya Lucaria.text: The Academy of Raya Lucaria sits in the middle of the great lake of Liurnia, and is the place of study for Glintstone Sorcerers. Long ago, Rennala charmed the Academy with her lunar magic. She became the Academy's master and established the house of Caria as royalty. However, when Rennala's husband Radagon left her to become the second Elden Lord, Rennala's heart went along with him. Those at the Academy then realised that Rennala was no champion, and she was confined to the great library. She still clutches the amber egg given to her by Radagon, which contains the Great Rune of the Unborn.

Ainsel River.text: One of the two great rivers that flow beneath the Lands Between. Ainsel is said to be the grave of civilisations that flourished before the Erdtree. The eastern side of Ainsel is dominated by the Uhl Palace Ruins, characterised by their mausoleums and statues, and inhabited by the Claymen who served as priests of the ancient dynasty.

Ancient Ruins of Rauh.text: Ancient ruins overgrown with lush, dense vegetation. The Rauh Ancient Ruins are the remains of a civilization that practiced the art of sprite magic, an art so ancient that even the Hornsent of antiquity had academics researching it.

Belurat, Tower Settlement.text: A Hornsent city at the base of a shaded tower, to the northwest of the Gravesite Plain. The Gate of Divinity is said to reside somewhere here. Belurat was besieged during the Crusade of Messmer the Impaler.

Caelid.text: A wasteland on the southeastern tip of the Lands Between, plagued by Scarlet Rot and inhabited by all manner of malformed creatures. Caelid borders Limgrave to its west. It was the site of the battle between General Radahn and Malenia, Blade of Miquella, during which the first flower of Aeonia bloomed and covered the region in Scarlet Rot. Radahn's army, the Redmanes, continues to combat the rot using fire.

Capital Outskirts.text: Leyndell, the city of the Erdtree, is a metropolis enclosed by double ramparts. The land surrounding the capital proper, within the outer wall, comprises the Capital Outskirts. During The Shattering, the Outskirts were ravaged by war, and the battlegrounds are still strewn with corpses. Wooden trebuchets lie in ruins, amidst abandoned encampments, and giant censers can be seen protruding from the ground.

Caria Manor.text: A large estate in the north-west of Liurnia. The manor was once the home of the Carian Royal Family, who ruled over Liurnia and governed the Academy of Raya Lucaria. After the Academy turned on the Carians, the Cuckoo Knights launched an assault on the manor, catching the Carian Knights off guard. However, the Cuckoos were caught in a magic snare which keeps their souls trapped within the manor.

Carian Study Hall.text: The Carian Study Hall is a building on the eastern coast of Liurnia, to the north of Jarburg. It is connected to the Divine Tower of Liurnia by a great bridge, though it is not accessible initially.

Castle Ensis.text: A looming castle to the north of the Gravesite Plain, across the Ellac Greatbridge from the main expanse. To the castle's west is Fog Rift, and to its north is Scadu Altus which can be reached from the Ensis Moongazing Grounds after defeating the castle's main boss.

Castle Morne.text: A large, heavily fortified castle that rises from the southern tip of the Weeping Peninsula. The castle was overseen by Castellan Edgar at the appointment of Godrick the Grafted. However, it has since been commandeered by its Misbegotten servants, who now control much of the castle. Castellan Edgar is one of the last holdouts, as nearby soldiers brawl with the Misbegotten.

Castle Sol.text: A castle in the northern Mountaintops of the Giants. The master of Castle Sol was once given half of a medallion that would allow him to visit Miquella's Haligtree. The castle was the site of an attempt to trigger an eclipse, in order to restore the soul of Miquella's comrade, however the sun was not swallowed and the master of the castle lost hope of ever seeing the Haligtree. Commander Niall, a veteran of Castle Sol, remained in the castle, commanding the spirits of his army of no nation to protect his long-passed master.

Central Altus.text: The Altus Plateau is a northwestern region of the Lands Between. It is a region of great significance, for it is here that the Erdtree can be found, as well as Leyndell, the royal capital of Queen Marika. Altus borders Liurnia of the Lakes to the south, and the Forbidden Lands which lead to the Mountaintops of the Giants to the east. Due to its high elevation, Altus is connected to its neighbouring regions primarily through two lifts; the Grand Lift of Dectus to the south and the Grand Lift of Rold to the east.

Central Liurnia.text: The westernmost region of the Lands Between. Characterized by its boggy woodlands, sheer cliffs, and pervasive mists, much of the region is sinking into the Liurnia Lake. On the eastern side of the region, the Liurnia Highway runs north to south, connecting the land to the Altus Plateau and Limgrave. The western coast is closely associated with the royal family of Caria, as it is the location of their stronghold in Caria Manor.

Cerulean Coast.text: A coastal plain of cerulean flowers and mist on the Southern Shore of the Realm of Shadow. Accessible by following the Ellac River downstream. The Cerulean Coast is adorned with massive stone coffins resembling ships. The region has ties to the traditions of the Lands Between from before the Age of the Erdtree regarding death; many of the roads in the Cerulean Coast are lined by spirit worms and jellyfish, and a ghostflame dragon can be found not far from the entrance to the area.

Charo's Hidden Grave.text: A field of crimson lilies nestled between the Cerulean Coast and the southern Gravesite Plain, and the resting place of Charo. It is said a rare gravesite flower blossoms here into the cold ghostflame. The silent ghostflame blooms that grow here are barely tangible, and are sisters to the spirit-calling grave violets.

Church District.text: Shadow Keep, Church District is a sub-section of the Shadow Keep.

Consecrated Snowfield.text: A snow-swept, misty area to the west of the Mountaintops of the Giants. The Consecrated Snowfield is final trial for those who seek Miquella's Haligtree, and can only be accessed by uniting the two halves of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, found in the Village of the Albinaurics and Castle Sol, and bringing them to the Grand Lift of Rold.

Crumbling Farum Azula.text: A giant ruined temple city in the sky, located above the sea to the east of the Lands Between. Once a royal city and the seat of the Dragonlord Placidusax, Farum Azula has been crumbling since time immemorial. Now, it is a mausoleum, guarded by chosen Beastmen who wield weapons clad in lightning. The storm beyond time rages in the center of the crumbling city, and at its heart is the Dragonlord's seat, where he awaits the return of his god.

Crumbling Farum Azula — Aftermath.text: A giant ruined temple city in the sky, located above the sea to the east of the Lands Between. Once a royal city and the seat of the Dragonlord Placidusax, Farum Azula has been crumbling since time immemorial. Now, it is a mausoleum, guarded by chosen Beastmen who wield weapons clad in lightning. The storm beyond time rages in the center of the crumbling city, and at its heart is the Dragonlord's seat, where he awaits the return of his god.

Deeproot Depths.text: An enormous cavern at the roots of the Erdtree, which is the source of the Ainsel and Siofra rivers. The network of roots that spread throughout the Lands Between also begins here.

East Altus.text: The Altus Plateau is a northwestern region of the Lands Between. It is a region of great significance, for it is here that the Erdtree can be found, as well as Leyndell, the royal capital of Queen Marika. Altus borders Liurnia of the Lakes to the south, and the Forbidden Lands which lead to the Mountaintops of the Giants to the east. Due to its high elevation, Altus is connected to its neighbouring regions primarily through two lifts; the Grand Lift of Dectus to the south and the Grand Lift of Rold to the east.

East Gravesite Plain.text: A vast sepulchral plain scattered with scorched ruins and ethereal spiritgraves, located in the south of the Realm of Shadow. The spiral tower of the Hornsent lies to the north-west of the region. The Gravesite Plain borders Scadu Altus to its east and the Land of the Tower to its west. The region is strewn with blackened ruins of the tower-folk, burned in the Crusade by the people of the Erdtree. The soldiers of Messmer the Impaler's army maintain a presence around the Church of Consolation, but are for the most part confined to the northern rim of the Ellac River canyon.

East Liurnia.text: The westernmost region of the Lands Between. Characterized by its boggy woodlands, sheer cliffs, and pervasive mists, much of the region is sinking into the Liurnia Lake. On the eastern side of the region, the Liurnia Highway runs north to south, connecting the land to the Altus Plateau and Limgrave. The western coast is closely associated with the royal family of Caria, as it is the location of their stronghold in Caria Manor.

East Mountaintops.text: The northern Mountaintops were once the home of the Fire Giants, after they claimed them from the ice dragons. At the birth of the Erdtree, the forces of Queen Marika the Eternal and Godfrey, First Elden Lord marched up the mountain and put the Giants to the sword. With the Giants defeated, the Flame of Ruin was confined within the Giants' Forge atop the mount, and the Age of the Erdtree began.

East Scadu Altus.text: A plateau in the center of the Realm of Shadow, occupied by the army of Messmer the Impaler. It was named for its counterpart in the realm of the Erdtree. Messmer's stronghold, the Shadow Keep, lies to the north of the region. In the eastern half of the plateau, the Recluses' River flows from the Castle Watering Hole and empties into the forbidden Abyssal Woods. The Ruins of Unte, the Village of Flies, and Bonny Village can be found along the Recluses' River.

Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.text: A jaded golden city to the north of the Lands Between. It is an optional endgame area that can only be reached by descending from Miquella's Haligtree, past Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree. The boss at the end of this area, deep within the city, is Malenia, Blade of Miquella.

Endings.text: Elden Ring features six total endings: Age of Fracture, Age of Order, Age of the Duskborn, Blessing of Despair, Age of the Stars and the Lord of Frenzied Flame.

Enir-Ilim.text: The fabled spiral tower of the Hornsent and the location of the Gate of Divinity, Enir-Ilim pierced the skies with such a majesty that it even inspired a secret faith in the people sent there to destroy it. When the Crusade of Messmer the Impaler took place, the tower was veiled in shadow. As such, Enir-Ilim may only be accessed after using Messmer's Kindling to burn the sealing tree located near the Church of the Bud in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh.

Enir-Ilim & DLC Finale.text: The fabled spiral tower of the Hornsent and the location of the Gate of Divinity, Enir-Ilim pierced the skies with such a majesty that it even inspired a secret faith in the people sent there to destroy it. When the Crusade of Messmer the Impaler took place, the tower was veiled in shadow. As such, Enir-Ilim may only be accessed after using Messmer's Kindling to burn the sealing tree located near the Church of the Bud in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh.

First steps in Limgrave.text: A temperate land of green plains and golden trees, with windswept hills to the north and a dense, mist-shrouded woodland to the east. Limgrave is the first open area encountered by the player after emerging from the Stranded Graveyard, located in the southwest of the Lands Between. It borders Liurnia to its northwest and Caelid to its northeast. In the south of Limgrave lies the Weeping Peninsula, an isolated region known for its unceasing rain.

Forbidden Lands.text: A dark, frigid stretch of land to the east of Leyndell, Royal Capital, which serves as a route to the Grand Lift of Rold and the northern Mountaintops of the Giants. This area only becomes accessible with the defeat of Morgott, the Omen King, when the player begins their journey to set the Erdtree aflame with Melina.

Fringefolk Hero's Grave.text: This Hero's Grave is connected to the Stranded Graveyard, locked behind a gate which requires two Stonesword Keys to open. This tomb is guarded by Chariot traps, spectral soldiers, and a pair of Grafted Scions.

Greyoll's Dragonbarrow.text: A large plateau to Caelids's north. Elder Dragon Greyoll and her children, the Dragons, made their nest here after escaping the Scarlet Rot, earning it it's name.

Jagged Peak.text: Visible from the rest of the Realm of Shadow, the great mountain can be seen dominating the skyline. The closer one gets to the mountain, the more dangerous and wild the storms become, and red lightning strikes the steep slopes and sharp stones. The area is home to many powerful dragons and drakes, and their corpses can be seen in great number littering the mountain's sides. At the top is a legendary and feared dragon, whose rage against the Dragonlord remains potent and destructive.

Lake of Rot.text: The Lake of Rot is a large cavernous area beneath Liurnia of the Lakes filled with rotting waters. The lake itself is littered with the crumbling remnants of an ancient dynasty. Within the center of the Lake of Rot are obelisks with stone pressure plates that when activated, raise platforms from beneath the lake, creating a pathway. In the southern part of this area, the Grand Cloister is found; a large walkway infested with rotted-flora and fauna.

Leyndell, Ashen Capital.text: With the defeat of Maliketh, the Black Blade, the Rune of Death is unbound, and the Flame of Ruin burns away the impenetrable thorns blocking the entrance to the Erdtree. The city of Leyndell is blanketed in thick ash, burying all but the tallest buildings. The Tarnished returns to the city after releasing the Rune of Death, finally able to approach the Erdtree and gain entry.

Leyndell, Royal Capital.text: The golden city at the foot of the Erdtree. Leyndell is the capital of the empire of the Golden Order. It is enclosed by double ramparts, with the city proper contained within the inner wall. To this day, the inner wall has never been breached. The current lord of Leyndell is Morgott, the Veiled Monarch, a Demigod of the Golden Lineage who took it upon himself to become the Erdtree's protector despite being born a graceless Omen.

Midra's Manse.text: A decaying manor hidden in the southern reaches of the forbidden Abyssal Woods and home to Sage Midra. The only way to access Midra's Manse is via traversing the madness-infested, swampy woodland.

Miquella's Haligtree.text: A holy tree created by Miquella off the northern coast of the Consecrated Snowfield. Miquella's Haligtree is a vast, misshapen tree in the far north of the Lands Between. Miquella's vision for the Haligtree was never fully realized, and even in their beauty, the town and city brace are teeming with danger.

Mohgwyn Palace.text: An island in the underground Siofra River, far to the east of Nokron, Eternal City. The grave of an ancient dynasty civilization can be found here, and it is in these ruins that Mohg, Lord of Blood, has chosen to be the seat of his coming Mohgwyn Dynasty.

Moonlight Altar.text: A plateau in the southwest of Liurnia, accessible only by passing through Ainsel River and the Lake of Rot and defeating Astel, Naturalborn of the Void. The lift which leads to the Moonlight Altar is sealed, and can only be accessed by obtaining the Dark Moon Ring from the treasure chest in Rennala's library in the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

Mt. Gelmir.text: Mt. Gelmir is a volcano in western Altus Plateau, home to the Volcano Manor at its summit. It is known for its sheer cliffs and ominous skies, qualities which grew more pronounced in the wake of The Shattering.

Nokron.text: One of the Eternal Cities inhabited by the Nox, who were banished underground after invoking the ire of the Greater Will. Nokron houses the Fingerslayer Blade, a blood-drenched fetish made from a corpse which can harm the Greater Will and its vassals, and is proof of the treason of the Nox.

Nokstella.text: One of the Eternal Cities inhabited by the Nox, who were banished underground after evoking the ire of the Greater Will. Nokstella is located in the Ainsel River Main, on the west side of the underground river Ainsel, and can only be accessed by using the sending gate in Renna's Rise and following the path through the northern Uhl Palace Ruins.

North Limgrave.text: A temperate land of green plains and golden trees, with windswept hills to the north and a dense, mist-shrouded woodland to the east. Limgrave is the first open area encountered by the player after emerging from the Stranded Graveyard, located in the southwest of the Lands Between. It borders Liurnia to its northwest and Caelid to its northeast. In the south of Limgrave lies the Weeping Peninsula, an isolated region known for its unceasing rain.

Rauh Base.text: A wetland in the canyon formed by the Scorpion River, far below the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. The eastern segment of Rauh Base is crossed by the great bridge between the Western Rampart of Shadow Keep and the Viaduct Minor Tower.

Recluses' River.text: The Recluses' River Shadow of the Erdtree is a river in the Realm of Shadow. It is not a strictly outlined region in-game, but it is a colloquially referenced sub-section of the Scadu Altus that is not accessible from anywhere else in the area. The river is physically separated from the rest of the region by its low elevation.

Redmane Castle.text: A fortress on an island to the south of Caelid, connected to the mainland by a heavily fortified greatbridge. The castle is the stronghold of General Radahn's army, beaten yet unbowed after their defeat at the hands of Malenia and her Cleanrot Knights.

Ruin-Strewn Precipice.text: A series of caves winding up the cliffs, joining Liurnia to the Altus Plateau. This dungeon can be used as an alternative route to the Grand Lift of Dectus in order to access Altus.

Scaduview.text: A rugged highland in the embrace of the Scadutree, just outside the back gate of Shadow Keep. The sub-region encompasses the Hinterland, the area surrounding the Scadutree Chalice, and the Finger Ruins of Dheo. Scaduview is the northernmost area in the Realm of Shadow, and the homeland of Queen Marika the Eternal.

Sellia.text: A town in Caelid on the eastern bank of the Swamp of Aeonia. Sellian sorcerers are assassins who are said to hunt their fellow sorcerers, employing night sorceries that allowed them to turn their weapons, or their own bodies, invisible to deceive their enemies.

Shadow Keep.text: The towering black keep, lair of Messmer the Impaler. Shadow Keep guards Scaduview to its north, the location of the Hinterland and the Scadutree. The keep itself has three main sections: the entrance's Main Gate Plaza, the Specimen Storehouse, and the Church District.

Siofra River.text: One of the two great rivers that flow beneath the Lands Between. Siofra is said to be the grave of civilisations that flourished before the Erdtree, and evidence of this can be found in the many ancient structures that litter the vast, subterranean space. The towering remains of an ancient dynasty are prominent throughout the area, inhabited by the Claymen who once served as the dynasty's priests.

South Liurnia.text: The westernmost region of the Lands Between. Characterized by its boggy woodlands, sheer cliffs, and pervasive mists, much of the region is sinking into the Liurnia Lake. On the eastern side of the region, the Liurnia Highway runs north to south, connecting the land to the Altus Plateau and Limgrave. The western coast is closely associated with the royal family of Caria, as it is the location of their stronghold in Caria Manor.

Stone Coffin Fissure.text: A massive underground ravine at the southernmost tip of the Realm of Shadow. The Stone Coffin Fissure is the place to which stone coffins drift. The chasm has taken on a bruised color from the putrescence oozing from the coffins; this putrescence is what remains of the "impure" life stored within each drifting coffin.

Stormveil Castle.text: Stormveil Castle perches atop a cliff overlooking Limgrave. Currently, it is the stronghold of the Demigod Godrick the Grafted, but long ago it was ruled over by an old king, back when the true storm raged. The castle is heavily guarded and patrolled by Banished Knights, Exile Soldiers, and warhawks with blades grafted to their talons. The exterior of the castle is mottled with craters lined with thorns, which have also spread to the soldiers within. It is said that the source may be hidden deep within the castle.

Subterranean Shunning-Grounds.text: An intricate system of sewers and dungeons that spreads out below Leyndell, Royal Capital. It is crawling with all kinds of shunned creatures, most notably the Omen, who are imprisoned there unbeknownst to anyone. The layout is disorienting due to the multitude of tunnels, waterways, and chambers. Deep within the dungeon is a cathedral, where an encounter with Mohg, the Omen occurs. The altar at the back of the cathedral is illusory, and hides a passage which can only be unsealed by killing Morgott, the Omen King in the city above.

The Shaded Castle.text: A derelict castle sinking into a poisonous mire in the north of Altus Plateau. For generations, the Shaded Castle was ruled over by House Marais, who served as both executioners and castellans. Maleigh Marais, born sickly like all sons of House Marais, became beguiled by Malenia, claiming to feel her presence when he held the Valkyrie's Prosthesis

Tutorial.text: The Tutorial of Elden Ring is shown throughout the game in the form of vignettes that inform the player of the mechanisms of the game. Hint & Tips are offered during loading screens and either provide new information or remind players of other tutorials.

Volcano Manor.text: The Volcano Manor is home to the recusants of Praetor Rykard, fierce warriors who wage war against the Erdtree and the Roundtable. The recusants are led by Rykard's consort, Lady Tanith. Powerful Tarnished are extended invitations to join the Volcano Manor and are given contracts to hunt other Tarnished in service of the Roundtable. Tarnished who prove themselves are offered an audience with Praetor Rykard himself, which will inevitably end with the serpentine demigod devouring them, making them forever a part of his "family".

Weeping Peninsula.text: The Weeping Peninsula is the southern-most tip of the Lands Between. The peninsula derives its name from its unceasing rainfall, giving the impression of a land in constant lament. It is connected to Limgrave proper by the Bridge of Sacrifice to its north.

West Altus.text: The Altus Plateau is a northwestern region of the Lands Between. It is a region of great significance, for it is here that the Erdtree can be found, as well as Leyndell, the royal capital of Queen Marika. Altus borders Liurnia of the Lakes to the south, and the Forbidden Lands which lead to the Mountaintops of the Giants to the east. Due to its high elevation, Altus is connected to its neighbouring regions primarily through two lifts; the Grand Lift of Dectus to the south and the Grand Lift of Rold to the east.

The spiral tower of the Hornsent lies to the north-west of the region. The Gravesite Plain borders Scadu Altus to its east and the Land of the Tower to its west. The region is strewn with blackened ruins of the tower-folk, burned in the Crusade by the people of the Erdtree. The soldiers of Messmer the Impaler's army maintain a presence around the Church of Consolation, but are for the most part confined to the northern rim of the Ellac River canyon.

It borders Liurnia to its northwest and Caelid to its northeast. In the south of Limgrave lies the Weeping Peninsula, an isolated region known for its unceasing rain.

Messmer's stronghold, the Shadow Keep, lies to the north of the region. In the eastern half of the plateau, the Recluses' River flows from the Castle Watering Hole and empties into the forbidden Abyssal Woods. The Ruins of Unte, the Village of Flies, and Bonny Village can be found along the Recluses' River.
